content: 1. Recommendations for Induced Abortion (<12 weeks gestation): A combination regimen of 200 mg of mifepristone taken orally once, followed by 800 μg of misoprostol administered vaginally, sublingually, or buccally is recommended. Alternatively, 800 μg of misoprostol alone can be used via the same routes. 2. Recommendations for Induced Abortion (≥12 weeks gestation): A combination regimen of 200 mg of mifepristone taken orally once, followed by 400 μg of misoprostol administered vaginally, sublingually, or buccally every 3 hours is recommended. Misoprostol alone can also be used in the same dosage and frequency. 3. Management of Missed Abortion (<14 weeks gestation): A combination regimen of 200 mg of mifepristone taken orally once, followed by 800 μg of misoprostol administered buccally, vaginally, or sublingually is recommended. Misoprostol alone can also be used in the same dosage and routes. 4. Management of Intrauterine Fetal Demise (≥14–28 weeks gestation): A combination regimen of 200 mg of mifepristone taken orally once, followed by 400 μg of misoprostol administered vaginally or sublingually every 4–6 hours is recommended. Sublingual administration of misoprostol is preferred, but vaginal administration is also acceptable. 5. Management of Incomplete Abortion (<14 weeks gestation, uterine size): 600 μg of misoprostol taken orally or 400 μg administered sublingually is recommended. 6. Management of Incomplete Abortion (≥14 weeks gestation, uterine size): 400 μg of misoprostol administered sublingually, vaginally, or buccally every 3 hours is recommended. 7. Induced Abortion (<12 weeks gestation) with Letrozole and Misoprostol: Letrozole 10 mg is taken orally daily for 3 days, followed by 800 μg of misoprostol administered sublingually on the fourth day. 8. Timing of Post-Abortion Contraception: Hormonal contraception can be initiated immediately after the first pill of a medical abortion. Intrauterine devices (IUDs) can be inserted after confirming the success of the abortion, typically 1–2 days later. 9. General Considerations for Misoprostol Use: The combination regimen of mifepristone and misoprostol is slightly more effective than misoprostol alone. There is no specific recommendation for a maximum number of doses, but healthcare providers should use clinical judgment, particularly in individuals with prior uterine incisions, as there is a rare risk of uterine rupture. For induced abortion beyond 24 weeks or intrauterine fetal demise beyond 28 weeks, the dose of misoprostol should be reduced due to limited data and increased uterine sensitivity to prostaglandins. Clinical judgment is essential in determining the appropriate dosage. 10. Uterine Growth During Pregnancy: After 4 weeks of gestation, the uterus increases in size by approximately 1 cm per week. By 12 weeks, the uterus rises out of the pelvis. At 15–16 weeks, the uterus reaches the midpoint between the symphysis pubis and the umbilicus. At 20 weeks, the uterus reaches the level of the umbilicus. 11. Pregnancy Dating: Pregnancy dating can be based on the last menstrual period (LMP) alone or in combination with a validated tool. If the LMP is uncertain, a clinical examination may be warranted. The least invasive method appropriate for the circumstances and available in the setting should be used. These recommendations are adapted from the Clinical Practice Handbook for Safe Abortion by the World Health Organization (2014) and other validated resources.
